title: CrFeVW<i>X</i> (<i>X</i> = Ta or Ti) High-Entropy Alloy: A Theoretical and Experimental Comparative Investigation on Phase Stability.

recollection.starting_material: GUESS: equiatomic mixture of elemental Cr, Fe, V, W and X (where X = Ta or Ti) powders
recollection.intervention: GUESS: preparation by arc‐melting under inert atmosphere followed by homogenization annealing; complementary density functional theory calculations using special quasi‐random structures to evaluate phase stability
recollection.structure: GUESS: predominantly single‐phase body‐centered cubic (BCC) solid solution for X = Ta; minor secondary hexagonal close‐packed (HCP) fraction (<5 %) when X = Ti
recollection.mechanism: GUESS: high configurational entropy stabilizes the BCC lattice; lattice distortion from atomic‐size mismatch and favorable negative mixing enthalpy further reinforce phase stability
recollection.results: GUESS: DFT‐computed mixing free energy ΔGmix ≈ –5 kJ/mol at 1000 K for Ta alloy, slightly less negative for Ti; experimentally, Vickers hardness ~450 HV (Ta) vs. ~380 HV (Ti), compressive yield strength ~1200 MPa (Ta) vs. ~900 MPa (Ti)

score.note: The recalled arc melting, annealing, and DFT/SQS workflow is incorrect; the paper used MD/hybrid MD-MC, ball milling, and SPS. The BCC assignment partially overlaps with the observed structures, but the claimed Ti HCP fraction is wrong and misses the Fe2Ta Laves phase and two BCC-type Ti-alloy phases. The entropy/size-mismatch explanation is generic, with only loose overlap with the actual Fe–Ta enthalpy mechanism. All reported energy, hardness, and strength values are fabricated and omit the actual lattice parameters, density, segregation temperatures, and thermal diffusivity.
